# The Stars That Never Move

## Scripture
*"God made two great lights—the greater light to govern the day and the lesser light to govern the night. He also made the stars. God set them in the vault of the sky to give light on the earth."* — Genesis 1:16–17 (NIV)

## Reflection
On a clear November evening, look toward the north. Find the Big Dipper, then follow its pointer stars to Polaris—the North Star. While everything else in the sky wheels slowly westward through the night, Polaris stays fixed. Sailors, shepherds, and travelers have trusted it for centuries.

But here's the wonder: Polaris doesn't actually stay still. It simply happens to sit almost directly above Earth's axis. The whole sky turns around it like a great celestial clock. And thousands of years from now, a different star will hold that place. What seems permanent to us is only a season in God's long story.

Genesis tells us God *set* the stars in place—not merely flung them into existence, but positioned them with care. Their apparent stillness is a gift: a fixed point so we can find our way. Yet even that fixed point will one day shift, because creation is not the Creator.

This is our comfort in a world of change. Jobs end, health falters, seasons pass. But the God who set the stars in the vault of the sky is the same yesterday, today, and forever. And the Light He placed there points us to something better than Polaris—to Jesus, the true Light who never shifts.

Tonight, let the North Star remind you: everything you can see will change. Trust the One who doesn't.

## Prayer
Lord, when everything around me feels uncertain, help me fix my eyes on You—the unchanging Light behind every changing star. Thank You for setting Your creation in place and for holding my life with the same care. Amen.
